name: Foundry Broadfoot Work Sneaker
description:
A wide-platform sneaker with a removable footbed system designed for augmented workers whose prosthetic feet are larger or differently weighted than standard shoe lasts accommodate. The toe box is unusually deep and wide, the outsole a chunky flat rubber platform. It comes in three widths and the insole stack is user-adjustable with included shims. Looks like an oversized utilitarian sneaker — functional ugliness worn with indifference.

The Foundry Broadfoot is the most common aug-compatible shoe on the Shelf and lower Tier 2. It's cheap, it works, and it doesn't pretend to be anything else.
functionality: Extra-wide, extra-deep toe box for large-format prosthetic feet. User-adjustable insole shim system for height and weight distribution compensation.
what_it_says: You're working class, augmented, and stretching every quanta. No shame in it.
worn_by: prosthetic users with non-standard foot profiles
people who can't afford fitted aug-footwear
story_hooks: The shim system is generic enough that people use Foundry footbeds to modify non-aug shoes — a small trade in modified footbeds exists on the Shelf.
A Foundry Broadfoot in good condition found at a crime scene is notable — it means the owner took care of things, which says something about them.
